# Backtest Report UI — Parameter Schema Contract

**Implements:** `GET /api/config/parameter_schema` (`backend/api/routes/config.py`), generated by
`backend/core/schema_introspection.py`, per Master Implementation Plan Phase 7 §7.1 / §5.2.1.

**Status:** the backend contract described here is built and verified. The frontend consumer
(`<ParameterReport>`, the six render rules, grouping/diff-mode/compare-drawer — Phase 7 items 7.2–7.7,
7.9–7.17) is **not built** — this document specifies the contract that work would consume, written now so
it doesn't drift from what the endpoint actually returns.

---

## 1. Why this exists

Master Plan §5.2.1: *"a single parameter schema, generated from the backend... kills the whole class of
frontend-label-drifted-from-backend-meaning bugs."* Before this endpoint, `Backtester.jsx` rendered
unknown/nested parameters via `JSON.stringify(v)` and maintained a hand-written `DEFAULT_FORM` literal
that could silently drift from `RiskParams`' real fields and defaults. This endpoint is generated
directly from the dataclasses that are ALSO what the risk/backtest engines actually read — there is no
second source of truth to drift from.

## 2. Endpoint

```
GET /api/config/parameter_schema
```

No authentication required — this describes the config SHAPE (field names, types, defaults, help text),
not any user's data.

Response:

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "key": "risk.max_margin_utilisation_pct",
      "group": "risk",
      "label": "Max margin utilisation pct",
      "type": "float",
      "unit": null,
      "help": "[2.1/A1] Ceiling on required margin as % of account equity...",
      "default": 30.0,
      "affects": []
    },
    {
      "key": "risk.be_mode",
      "group": "risk",
      "label": "Be mode",
      "type": "enum",
      "unit": null,
      "help": "[5.1/5.3/Part4] `RR` ignores `tp1_hit`...",
      "default": "EITHER",
      "affects": [],
      "enum_options": ["RR", "TP_HIT", "EITHER", "NONE"]
    }
  ]
}
```

As of this writing: **219 fields** across **9 groups** (`risk`, `prop_firm`, `apa`, `vwap`, `crt`,
`htf_fvg_flip`, `bias_ifvg`, `ny_open_retest`, `drift_jump_alpha`) — regenerated automatically as fields
are added/removed/redocumented; this count will drift from the source dataclasses over time by design.

## 3. Field object contract

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | `"{group}.{field_name}"` — matches how the field is actually addressed in a saved `UserConfigV2` (e.g. `config.risk.max_margin_utilisation_pct`). |
| `group` | string | One of the 9 dataclass groups above. Matches the `UserConfigV2` attribute name (`config.risk`, `config.vwap`, ...) — **not** the Phase 7 §7.5 display grouping (Run / Account & Prop Firm / Risk & Sizing / ...), which is a UI-layer concern the frontend still owns. |
| `label` | string | Auto-generated from the field name (`snake_case` → `Title Case`, e.g. `be_mode` → "Be mode"). Not hand-curated — expect awkward capitalisation on acronym-heavy names (`vwap_bands_enabled` → "Vwap bands enabled"); a future pass could special-case a small acronym list if this matters for the UI. |
| `type` | string | One of `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `enum`, `list`, `map`. Derived from the Python type annotation, unwrapping `X \| None` to `X`. |
| `unit` | string \| null | **Always `null` today.** Units are not currently annotated on `RiskParams`/strategy `Params` fields in a machine-readable way (they live in prose inside each field's docstring, e.g. "in pips", "as % of balance"). Populating this properly needs a structured annotation convention this codebase doesn't have yet — flagged, not guessed. |
| `help` | string | Extracted from the field's own **attribute docstring** — the plain string literal immediately following the field assignment in the dataclass source (the same convention Sphinx's `autodoc` reads for the same reason). This is the ACTUAL engineering rationale already written throughout `config_schema.py` and every strategy's `params.py` — nothing paraphrased or re-derived. Empty string when a field has no such docstring. |
| `default` | any | The dataclass field's real default value (including `default_factory`-produced defaults, e.g. `tp_splits`'s `[50.0, 30.0, 20.0]`). |
| `affects` | list | **Always `[]` today.** Specified in the plan (`{"affects": [...]}` — e.g. `["sizing"]`) but no source of truth for which subsystems a field affects exists in this codebase (it would need per-field tagging that doesn't exist) — flagged, not guessed, same as `unit`. |
| `enum_options` | list[string] | Only present when `type == "enum"` (i.e. the field's annotation is `Literal[...]`). The exact set of valid values. |

## 4. Grouping order (§7.5 — not yet implemented)

The plan specifies a fixed DISPLAY order distinct from the `group` field above: *Run · Account & Prop
Firm · Risk & Sizing · Targets & Exits · Strategy Parameters · Costs (resolved) · Advanced*, collapsed by
default except Run and Risk & Sizing. This endpoint does not attempt that grouping — `group` is the
dataclass name, a stable machine key; mapping dataclass groups (and probably individual fields within
`risk`) to the display categories is a frontend-layer decision that belongs in the `<ParameterReport>`
component (Phase 7.2), not baked into the API contract.

## 5. Known gaps / follow-up

- `unit` and `affects` are always empty — see the table above for why.
- `label` is mechanically generated, not curated — some will read awkwardly in a real UI.
- No `resolved_cost_model` special-casing (§7.4 wants a dedicated Symbol/Spread/Slippage/... table for
  that specific nested structure) — this endpoint treats every field uniformly; a resolved-cost-model
  view is a frontend rendering-rule concern (§7.3's six render rules), not a schema-shape concern.
- The frontend consumer (`<ParameterReport>`, diff mode, compare drawer, `Backtester.jsx::DEFAULT_FORM`
  pointed at this endpoint) is unbuilt — see `implementation/TASKS.md` Phase 7 for the itemised remainder.
